items.body:
#### What type of PR is this?

/kind cleanup

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

This adds a generic implementation of the default client-go methods (`Get`, `List` etc.), and uses them instead of the template code in generated clients. This reduces the amount of generated code, and more importantly IMO, extracts the default implementation into a Go file (which can more readily be read, analyzed, modified, tested...). As a result, clientsets with no extensions are reduced to their main getter, their interface, their specific struct, and their constructor. All method implementations are provided by the generic implementation. The dedicated interface is preserved so that each clientset can have its own set of methods, and the dedicated struct is preserved to allow extensions and expansions to be defined where necessary.

This requires exporting a method from generated `ApplyConfiguration` objects; the current implementation of that change isn’t great and will be refined if the overall direction of this PR seems useful. Similarly, I added a dummy method to check that extensions on the main resource aren’t affected; this should be turned into a proper test.

Significantly, the external interface of generated clientsets doesn’t change as a result of this PR: the return type is still the non-generic interface, and each getter still returns a pointer to a non-generic struct.

#### Which issue(s) this PR fixes:
